hero.title: Repairing vs Scrapping The Financial Decision Guide 2026
hero.description: The £4,000-£8,000 rule: If repair or replacement cost exceeds 50-70% of vehicle value , consider scrapping. Repair: £50-£2,000+ · Replacement: £2,000-£6,000+ · Scrap value: £100-£500

blocks.text: 🔒 Secure enquiry · genuine quotes · UK-wide network.

This guide is based on 24,650 real UK engine replacement quote requests submitted through Engines Market between January and December 2025, aggregated pricing from 100+ UK suppliers , vehicle valuation data from Parkers, AutoTrader, and CAP HPI, and workshop interviews with 100+ engine specialists .

cards.title: Dataset insight
cards.text: "The emotional attachment to a vehicle often leads owners to over-invest in repairs. The objective financial threshold - repair cost vs vehicle value - is frequently ignored, resulting in poor financial outcomes. The 50-70% rule is the dominant decision logic in the UK engine industry: if repair or replacement cost exceeds 50-70% of vehicle value, scrapping is often the better financial decision."
cards.meta: Source: Repairing vs Scrapping Financial Decision Guide (2026), Engines Market. Based on 24,650 UK engine replacement quote requests (Jan-Dec 2025). [EM-VERIFIED]

ordered.title: The sunk cost fallacy - why owners over-invest

blocks.text: "I've had this car for years - it's worth saving no matter the cost."
Every car has a financial point of no return. When repair costs approach or exceed vehicle value, you're not repairing - you're buying the car again.

The sunk cost fallacy: • You've spent £2,000 on repairs last year • You've owned the car for 8 years • You're emotionally attached None of this changes the financial reality: spending £3,500 on a £4,000 car is poor economics. [EM-OBSERVED]

"In the UK engine industry, the 50-70% rule is the dominant decision logic: if repair or replacement cost exceeds 50-70% of vehicle value, scrapping is often the better financial decision. The emotional attachment to a vehicle is the biggest obstacle to making a rational choice."
[EM-OBSERVED] based on 24,650 quote requests and owner behaviour analysis.
